statement_en:
Consider
$$f(x,y):=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{y^2}&0<x<y<1\\
-\frac{1}{x^2}&0<y<x<1 \\ 0 &\text{ otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Let $I=[0,1]$. Show first that
$$\int_I\int_I |f(x,y)|\,dydx=+\infty,$$
so $f$ is not integrable and Fubini's theorem does not apply. Conclude that one should expect
$$\int_I\int_I f(x,y)dydx \neq \int_I\int_I f(x,y)dxdy.$$
final_code:
import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal

noncomputable section

def f (x y : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if 0 < x ∧ x < y ∧ y < 1 then
    1 / y ^ 2
  else if 0 < y ∧ y < x ∧ x < 1 then
    -(1 / x ^ 2)
  else
    0

def I : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1

theorem mainTheorem :
    (∫⁻ x in I, ∫⁻ y in I, ENNReal.ofReal (|f x y|) ∂volume ∂volume) = ∞ ∧
    ¬ Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => f p.1 p.2) ∧
    (∫ x in I, ∫ y in I, f x y ∂volume ∂volume) ≠
      (∫ y in I, ∫ x in I, f x y ∂volume ∂volume) := by
  sorry
